Start a line with a name and a colon (Office: 52.5163, 13.3777) to see that name in the results. Valhalla needs coordinates: to start from an address, look it up first with OpenStreetMap Nominatim and pass its result here.

parameters.name: stops

parameters.description: Finish back at the first stop, for a round trip. Off by default, which keeps your last stop last.
parameters.name: return_to_start

parameters.description: How the trip is made. Car by default. Each mode keeps to the roads and paths open to it: a truck avoids roads closed to heavy vehicles, a bicycle prefers cycle lanes, walking uses footpaths.
parameters.name: travel_mode

parameters.description: Kilometres or miles for every distance in the result. Kilometres by default.
parameters.name: units

parameters.description: The language the turn-by-turn instructions are written in. English (United States) by default.
parameters.name: language

parameters.description: Kinds of road to stay off where there is another way. Valhalla still uses one when nothing else gets there. Toll roads and motorways only matter to motor vehicles.
parameters.name: avoid

parameters.description: Return the route's line as coordinates and as GeoJSON, ready for a map. On by default. Turn it off for long routes when only the distance, time and directions are needed; the encoded polyline is always returned.
parameters.name: include_geometry

bounding_box.description: The smallest box around the line or area. Empty when there is none.

coordinates.description: The line as [latitude, longitude] pairs. Empty when 'Include the line' is off.

directions_text.description: Every instruction as numbered lines with its distance, ready to put in a message.

distance.description: The total distance, in the units asked for.

distance_text.description: The total distance in words, such as '2.7 km'.

duration_seconds.description: The total travel time, in seconds.

duration_text.description: The total travel time in words, such as '7 min' or '1 h 5 min'.

encoded_polyline.description: The whole line as an encoded polyline with six decimal places, which the GPS trace and elevation actions take as input.

geojson.description: The line as a GeoJSON Feature (a LineString, [longitude, latitude] order) for a map. Empty when 'Include the line' is off.

has_ferry.description: Whether the trip takes a ferry.

has_highway.description: Whether the trip uses a motorway or highway.

has_toll.description: Whether the trip uses a toll road.

legs.description: Each part of the trip between two stops.

distance.description: The leg's length, in the units asked for.

distance_text.description: The leg's length in words, such as '2.7 km'.

duration_seconds.description: How long the leg takes, in seconds.

duration_text.description: How long the leg takes in words, such as '7 min'.

from_label.description: The stop the leg starts from.

maneuver_count.description: How many instructions the leg has.

position.description: Which leg of the trip this is, from 1.

to_label.description: The stop the leg ends at.

distance.description: How far to go after the instruction, in the units asked for.

duration_seconds.description: How long that part takes, in seconds.

instruction.description: The written instruction, such as 'Turn right onto Alexanderstraße.'

kind.description: What kind of move it is, such as start, turn_left, turn_right, slight_right, roundabout_enter, ferry_enter or destination.

leg.description: Which leg of the trip it belongs to, from 1.

step.description: The instruction's number across the whole trip, from 1.

travel_type.description: The vehicle or way of travel for this part, such as car, foot or hybrid (a bicycle).

optimized_order.description: The best order, as the positions the stops had in your list: [1, 3, 2, 4] means visit your third stop second.

order_text.description: The stops' names in the best order, such as 'A, then C, then B'.

stops.description: The stops, in the order they are visited.

input_position.description: Where this stop was in the list you gave, from 1.

label.description: The stop's name, or its coordinates when it was given no name.

position.description: Where this stop comes in the trip, from 1.

side_of_street.description: Which side of the street the stop is on when you arrive or leave: 'left' or 'right'. Empty when it sits on the road itself.

summary.description: One readable sentence saying what came back.

travel_mode.description: The travel mode used: auto (car), bicycle, pedestrian (walking), truck, motor_scooter, motorcycle, bus or taxi.

warnings.description: Notes about how the trip was planned, if any.

description: Plan routes on OpenStreetMap data with Valhalla, the open-source routing engine behind the directions on openstreetmap.org, through the free public server run by FOSSGIS. Get turn-by-turn directions by car, bicycle, on foot, by truck, motorcycle or bus in 29 languages, put a round of stops in the quickest order, work out travel times between many places, map the area reachable within a time or distance, find the nearest road and its speed limit, get elevations along a line, match GPS traces to roads, and find a fair meeting point. Places are given as latitude and longitude. No account or API key required.
